title: DPI scaling
description:
Scale sizes for high-DPI screens.

```
96 dpi (100%):   button 100x30 -> 100x30
144 dpi (150%):  button 100x30 -> 150x45
192 dpi (200%):  font 9 pt -> 24 px
moved from 144 to a 120 dpi monitor: window 1500x900 -> 1250x750
```
hints: `MulDiv` computes in 64 bits and rounds to the nearest: `(std::int64_t{a} * b + c / 2) / c` for positive values (lesson 3.04).
`WM_DPICHANGED` gives the new DPI and a suggested rectangle; use that rectangle rather than computing your own.
requirements: Font points to pixels: `-MulDiv(points, dpi, 72)` (negative height means character height).
On a DPI change, rescale from the old DPI to the new one.
stretch: Handle negative values in `mulDiv` the way the real one rounds them.
